prompt:
Silicon nanosphere, 150 nm in diameter, in air, illuminated with 2.0 eV photons. What's its scattering efficiency Q_sca? Please use the bundled crystalline silicon data.

---
Report your result by calling submit_answer with these values:
- `q_sca` (dimensionless): scattering efficiency C_sca / (pi r^2)

concerns: I converted 2.0 eV to a vacuum wavelength of 619.92 nm using hc = 1239.84 eV·nm.
I used the bundled crystalline silicon data (Green 2008, the default), which gives n = 3.898 + 0.0174i at this wavelength. I assumed plane-wave illumination.

At this size and wavelength the sphere is close to its magnetic-dipole resonance, so Q_sca is sensitive to the exact diameter and to the silicon dataset used. Small changes in either could shift it noticeably.
answer.summary: The scattering efficiency of a 150 nm silicon sphere in air at 2.0 eV (619.92 nm) is Q_sca ≈ 7.16. I calculated it with exact Mie theory using the bundled crystalline silicon data (Green 2008), which gives n = 3.898 + 0.0174i at this wavelength. The scattering cross-section is C_sca = 126,551 nm², and dividing by πr² = 17,671 nm² gives the efficiency. For context, the extinction efficiency is Q_ext ≈ 8.01 and the absorption cross-section is about 14,974 nm², so about 89% of the extinction is scattering.

ConstantIndex.description: Wavelength-independent complex refractive index n + ik.

ConstantIndex.title: ConstantIndex

Cylinder.description: Flat-ended cylinder with axis along z.

Drude.description: eps(w) = eps_inf - wp^2 / (w^2 + i*gamma*w), energies in eV.

DrudeLorentz.description:
eps(w) = eps_inf - wp^2/(w^2 + i g w) + sum_j d_j w0_j^2 / (w0_j^2 - w^2 - i G_j w).

The form FDTD needs for auxiliary-differential-equation dispersion.
Fit one to measured data with :func:`lightsmith.materials_fit.fit_drude_lorentz`.
DrudeLorentz.title: DrudeLorentz

FarFieldRequest.description:
Differential scattering cross section dC_sca/dOmega on a theta x phi grid.

theta is measured from the incident direction; phi is the azimuth around it,
measured from the incident polarization (phi=0 is the E-plane, 90 the H-plane).
FarFieldRequest.title: FarFieldRequest

GaussianBeam.description:
A focused Gaussian beam: plane waves with the angular spectrum exp(-(k_t w0 / 2)^2), each polarised by
rotating `polarization` with its direction (aplanatic).

The angular weights are fixed, so the beam behaves as if focused by a lens of fixed NA: the waist is
`waist_nm` at `waist_wavelength_nm` (default: the middle of the band) and scales with the wavelength.
Cross sections are normalised by the intensity at the focus.

waist_wavelength_nm.description: Vacuum wavelength at which the waist is waist_nm. Default: the middle of the band.
waist_wavelength_nm.title: Waist Wavelength Nm

GaussianBeam.title: GaussianBeam

LayeredSphere.description:
Core-shell / multilayer sphere. The particle's `material` is the core;
`shells` are listed from the inside out.

result.conventions:
Lightsmith conventions (fixed; changing them needs a schema version bump):
- Lengths in nm. Wavelengths are vacuum wavelengths in nm.
- Time dependence exp(-i omega t): absorbing materials have Im(eps) > 0 and Im(n) > 0.
- Cross sections in nm^2; efficiencies Q = C / (pi r_eq^2), r_eq = volume-equivalent radius of all particles.
- layer_stack / periodic: layers listed from the superstrate (incidence side) to the substrate; light travels +z.
  R is measured in the superstrate, T in the substrate.
- mode: cross-section in the xy plane, propagation along +z.
- device: ports are planes whose normal is the axis where size_nm is zero; direction is into the device.
- problem.options[<method or backend name>] holds solver options, validated by that backend.
- Materials: {"kind": "constant_index", "n_real": .., "n_imag": ..}, {"kind": "library", "name": "Au"},
  drude, drude_lorentz, tabulated, constant_permittivity. FDTD needs dispersive models (fit_drude_lorentz).
- Results carry provenance and warnings: read the warnings before trusting the numbers.

input.summary: The scattering efficiency of a 150 nm silicon sphere in air at 2.0 eV (619.92 nm) is Q_sca ≈ 7.16. I calculated it with exact Mie theory using the bundled crystalline silicon data (Green 2008), which gives n = 3.898 + 0.0174i at this wavelength. The scattering cross-section is C_sca = 126,551 nm², and dividing by πr² = 17,671 nm² gives the efficiency. For context, the extinction efficiency is Q_ext ≈ 8.01 and the absorption cross-section is about 14,974 nm², so about 89% of the extinction is scattering.
